subject: Clarify pilot: no-training carveout, subprocessors & APAC routing
messages:
From: Samantha Lewis <samantha.lewis@acmepharm.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: legal@acmepharm.com
Date: Fri, 16 Feb 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Pilot DPA questions – no-training & APAC routing

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — team was impressed with the latency profile. Legal ran through our pilot DPA and flagged a few items we need clarified before procurement signs off:

- No-training / no-model-improvement: Acme needs an explicit commitment that data collected during the pilot will not be used to improve or fine-tune any model (including internal experiments) unless we give written consent.
- Prompt/response ownership: we need the output (responses generated by the model) to be licensed to Acme for our product; we also need clarity on derivative/redistribution rights.
- Subprocessors & APAC residency: can you confirm the subprocessors that will process Acme tenant data during the pilot, and whether any telemetry, logs, or backups will cross APAC borders? We prefer APAC residency for logs/backup and KMS.
- Evidence & timing: SOC2 report and an ops attestation would be helpful before we start.

I've attached our redlined DPA (Acme_DPA_redlines_v1.pdf). Can you coordinate with legal and privacy? We hope to start a two-week pilot week of Mar 5, so timing is tight.

Appreciate a short call if easier.

Cheers,
Samantha Lewis
Senior PM, Platform Integrations
Acme Pharmaceuticals

Attachments: Acme_DPA_redlines_v1.pdf (pdf)

Hi Samantha — thanks for the clear note and the redlines.

Short answer up front: we can support a scoped no-training commitment for the pilot and put APAC residency measures in place, but a couple of operational constraints will need to be explicit in the addendum. Looping in Kim (legal) and David (privacy/ops) to propose precise language and evidence.

Suggested immediate steps:
- Legal addendum: Redwood will draft a one-page addendum that defines the pilot scope (tenants, date range, and telemetry types) and a no-model-improvement commitment limited to that scope.
- Subprocessor list & routing: we'll provide the current subprocessors and a routing plan that pins logs/backups to the APAC region for the pilot (or offer a Dedicated/Private deployment to guarantee it).
- Evidence: we can share our most recent SOC2 Type II and a short ops attestation (2–3 pages).
- Call: propose 30 min Tues Feb 20 at 10am PT to walk through the redlines and confirm the M.A.P. (mutual action plan).

I'll attach our draft addendum and the mutual action plan after Kim weighs in.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz

Subject: Re: Pilot DPA questions – no-training & APAC routing

Thanks Vanessa / Samantha — quick legal summary and proposed language.

1) No-training commitment
We can accept a scoped "no-model-improvement" commitment for the pilot period provided the following are included in the addendum:
- Scope: tenant-specific (Acme tenant IDs: to be listed) and time-boxed (start/end dates).
- Exclusions: system telemetry and aggregated, de-identified metrics used for performance monitoring will continue to be collected; any use of raw prompt/response material for training requires separate written consent.
- Verification: Redwood will provide an ops attestation describing retention windows, KV cache policies, and the controls to prevent pipeline ingestion into training workflows.

Proposed clause snippet (draft):
"During the Pilot Period, Redwood Inference will not use Acme's tenant data or generated outputs to train, fine-tune, or otherwise improve any machine learning models outside of the Production model instance expressly provisioned for the Pilot. Administrative telemetry necessary for service stability (system metrics, aggregated latency statistics) may be collected in de-identified form and will not be used for model training. Any use beyond this scope requires prior written consent from Acme"

2) Prompt/response ownership
- Redwood will grant Acme a perpetual, royalty-free, worldwide license to use, reproduce, and distribute outputs generated during the Pilot for Acme's internal product purposes; Redwood will retain rights to use anonymized, aggregated telemetry for service improvement. If Acme requires exclusive ownership of outputs, we need to route to a Private deployment or include additional licensing language (we can discuss).

3) Subprocessors & APAC residency
- We'll provide our subprocessors list and highlight any that process logs outside APAC. For the pilot we can either: (a) route logs/backups to APAC region endpoints (best-effort on Hosted) or (b) provision a Dedicated/Private environment to guarantee residency.
- If Acme needs 100% subprocessor onshore for APAC, Dedicated/Private is the safer path.

4) Evidence
- SOC2 Type II (most recent) and a 2-page ops attestation are available; we will prepare a short appendix with KMS residency options and a high-level runbook for retention/deletion.

Next steps from our side: we'll convert Vanessa's draft to a redline-ready addendum and circulate it by EOD Mon Feb 19. Marissa, can you coordinate scheduling and the HubSpot deal update? David, please confirm the technical routing options for APAC (hosted routing vs dedicated).

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

On verification: attachments referenced by Acme will be reviewed by legal; any proposed exclusive ownership language will need more detailed procurement review.
